비 오는 날 호송을 맡았던 일행에게서 소식이 온다. 당신이 앞장서 길을: News arrives from the group you escorted on a rainy day. They say they reached their destination safely thanks to you leading the way. Now, they offer to lead the way for you.
It was a wet path, but this time you could walk behind. Your breathing felt much easier.
그들은 고개를 숙이고 돌아갔다. 빚이라고 생각하지 않는 것이 서로 편했다: They bowed their heads and left. It was easier for both sides not to consider it a debt.
비 오는 날 호송에서 뒤만 따라 걸었던 일이 떠오른다. 그때 앞장섰던 사: You recall the rainy day escort where you only followed behind. They say the person who led the way back then returned injured. The rumor has only just reached your ears.
그는 괜찮다고 했지만 한쪽 어깨를 오래 문질렀다. 오래 앉아 있다 돌아왔: He said he was fine, but he rubbed one shoulder for a long time. You left after sitting for a while.
It became a forgotten matter. It only comes to mind occasionally on rainy days.
오래전 답장을 보냈던 사람에게서 다시 편지가 왔다. 필체는 그대로인데 봉: A letter arrived again from someone you wrote back to long ago. The handwriting is the same, but the envelope is worn. In that time, both the City and you have changed a lot.
There wasn't much to say. Just regards, the weather, and a name.
You did not write a reply. Instead, you placed the letter in the driest drawer.
서랍을 정리하다 오래전 넣어 둔 편지를 찾았다. 봉투는 누렇게 변했고,: While tidying the drawer, you found a letter put away long ago. The envelope has turned yellow, and you don't even know if the person you would write to is still there.
There was a brief regard in the last line. It was a regard that would no longer reach anyone.
You will read it someday. It’s just that that "someday" never comes.
게시판에 낯익은 전단이 또 붙었다. 몇 해 전 쫓아가 잡았던 사람의 일행: A familiar flyer is posted on the bulletin board again. They say it's an associate of the person you chased and caught a few years ago. The bounty is larger than last time.
The face on the flyer slowly turned around at the end of the alley. It seemed they were waiting.
신고했던 골목: The alley where you reported it
신고만 하고 지나쳤던 골목에서 누군가 당신을 알아본다. 전단 속 얼굴의: Someone recognizes you in the alley where you once just made a report and passed by. It's an acquaintance of the face on the flyer. Their gaze is not kind.
상대는 한참 노려보다 먼저 시선을 돌렸다. 돈 몇 푼을 쥐여 주고 사라졌: The other person stared for a long while before looking away first. They shoved a few coins into your hand and disappeared.
You were grabbed by the collar. You barely managed to escape.
You took a long way around. The gaze from behind followed you to the very end.
예전에 사들인 유품과 같은 각인이 있는 칼집을 든 사람이 찾아온다. 주인: A person carrying a scabbard with the same engraving as a keepsake you bought a long time ago comes looking for you. They say they are the owner's family. You could return it if they pay the price.
The family member silently took the scabbard and held it to their chest. You decided not to accept payment.
You handed it over to someone who offered the full price. The family member stood there for a long time before leaving.
골목 시장에서 예전에 지나쳤던 유품이 다시 나왔다. 그때보다 값이 많이: A keepsake you passed by before has appeared in the alley market again. The price has dropped significantly since then. It seems no one bought it.
Your eye for it was right this time. After reselling it, the price went up.
Even after haggling, it was a fake.
You never touched the belongings of the dead until the end.
밤새 일손을 거들었던 공방에서 사람이 찾아온다. 주인이 장비 한 번 손봐: Someone from the workshop where you helped out overnight comes looking for you. The owner says they will fix your gear once.
The owner was a person of few words, but their hands were precise. The gear you received back felt light.
Instead, the owner left an envelope of money, saying it was for that day's work.
하청 일손을 사양했던 공방이 문을 닫았다는 소문이 들린다. 주인은 어디론: Rumor has it that the workshop that declined your subcontracting help has closed its doors. They say the owner left for somewhere.
A single tool remained on the dust-covered workbench.
It was just a path you were passing through.
인파 속에서 같은 얼굴이 다시 지나간다. 오래전 말을 걸어 보았던 그 얼: The same face passes by again in the crowd. It is that face you tried speaking to long ago. This time, the other person stops walking first.
It was a short greeting, but you confirmed that you were both in the same City.
A nod was returned. That was enough.
인파 속에서 낯익은 얼굴이 다시 보인다. 오래전 고개를 숙이고 지나친 그: A familiar face is seen again in the crowd. It is that face that bowed and passed by long ago. It seems they recognized you too.
The other person looked surprised but soon smiled. A few trivial words were exchanged.
You passed the same path in the same way.
어느 날 여러 사람이 당신 이름을 기억하고 있다는 걸 알게 된다. 병원: One day, you realize that many people remember your name. There are people nodding in front of the hospital, at the market, and at the end of the alley. Faces whose names you don't know are mixed in.
Greetings invited more greetings. Your steps felt light all year long.
모른 척 지나간다: Pass by pretending not to notice
You hurried your steps out of awkwardness. Still, the gaze behind your back was warm.
한때 가까웠던 얼굴이 인사를 받지 않는다. 당신이 한 일이 어디선가 말이: A face that was once close does not return your greeting. It seems what you did is being talked about somewhere.
An awkward conversation was exchanged. Nothing was resolved, but the connection wasn't broken.
No answer came back. All that remained in your hands was the cold air.
You left the cold hands cold. One familiar face has been lost.
지나친 일들이 하나씩 떠오르는 밤이 있다. 잘못이라고 할 만한 것은 아니: There are nights when the things you passed by come to mind one by one. They aren't exactly mistakes. Still, memory is as accurate as a ledger.
다음 날 한 번쯤은 나선다: Step out at least once the next day
You helped with a small matter in the alley. One line in the ledger changed.
Sleep came. The ledger remains the same.
어제까지 있던 가게의 간판이 오늘은 없다. 벽에는 간판 모양으로 덜 바랜: The sign of the shop that was there until yesterday is gone today. Only a less-faded mark in the shape of the sign remains on the wall. In this City, shops and people disappear like this.
자국을 한참 본다: Look at the mark for a long time
이름은 몰라도 그 가게의 냄새는 기억났다. 기억이 있는 한 완전히 사라진: Even if you didn't know the name, you remembered the scent of that shop. As long as there is memory, it hasn't completely disappeared.
옆집 주인이 대답했다. 이 도시에서는 묻는 쪽이 더 오래 산다. 사례 삼: The owner next door answered. In this City, the one who asks lives longer. You handed them a small amount of money as a token of thanks.
골목 끝에 새 비석이 서 있다. 이름 칸은 비어 있고, 아래에는 이렇게만: A new tombstone stands at the end of the alley. The name space is empty, and below it, only this is written: For those whom this City remembers.
손을 얹고 눈을 감는다: Place your hand on it and close your eyes
The tombstone was cold. A moment later, something inside you settled down.
이름 칸에 내 이름을 새긴다: Carve your name in the name space
칼끝이 돌에 닿는 소리가 멀리까지 갔다. 이름은 새겼지만, 비석에 새겨진: The sound of the blade tip touching the stone traveled far. You carved your name, but they say the name carved on a tombstone is the first to be forgotten.
There are too many tombstones in this City that have no business being here.
어린 얼굴이 문 앞에 서서 당신의 이름을 부른다. 누구에게서 이름을 들었: A young face stands before the door and calls your name. They do not say who told them your name. They only mimic the way you hold your blade.
아이는 한 번 보고 따라 했다. 가르치는 동안 당신도 오래 잊었던 동작: The child watched once and followed suit. While teaching, you recovered a move you had long forgotten.
The child bowed their head and left. Muddy footprints remained on the threshold for a long time.
아이의 칼은 가벼웠지만 곧았다. 몇 합 뒤 당신 쪽이 먼저 손을 거두었다: The child's blade was light but straight. After a few exchanges, you were the first to lower your weapon.
The child's blade grazed your arm. It had been a long time since you felt like laughing.
오래전 함께 일하던 이의 유품 상자가 도착했다. 보낸 사람 이름은 없고,: A box of keepsakes from someone you worked with long ago has arrived. There is no sender's name, only your name written on the box.
안에는 낡은 장갑과 접힌 지도가 있었다. 지도에는 아직 가지 못한 골목이: Inside were worn gloves and a folded map. The map marks alleys you have yet to visit.
열지 않은 상자는 오래 그대로 있다. 열지 않았기에 아직 그 사람은 어딘: The unopened box has remained the same for a long time. Because it was never opened, it feels as if that person is still out there somewhere.
The smoke rose straight up. That is a rare sight in this City.
시장 사람들이 당신을 보면 말을 멈춘다. 가격표는 있지만 값은 사람마다: The market people stop talking when they see you. There are price tags, but the price changes depending on the person. This City sells things at a higher price to those who have lived here longer.
Between folding and unfolding two fingers, the price was cut in half.
The merchant smiled and doubled the price.
The market is not honest, but it saves time.
Walking away empty-handed is also a skill.
벽에 붙은 현상 전단 속 얼굴이 낯익다. 눈매가 닮았다. 아니, 정확히는: The face on the wanted poster on the wall looks familiar. The eyes are similar. No, to be precise, they are the eyes you saw in the mirror.
The paper was unexpectedly thick. There was a note from someone on the back.
A name posted by someone else should be removed by someone else.
전단을 붙인 자를 찾는다: Find the person who posted it
골목 그림자 속에서 풀칠한 손을 찾아냈다. 그 손은 아무 말 없이 도망쳤: You found the glue-stained hands in the shadows of an alley. The hands ran away without a word.
The shadow moved first. You missed them.
한 구역이 소리도 없이 가라앉고 있다. 사람들이 짐을 들고 지나간다. 누: A district is sinking without a sound. People pass by carrying their luggage. No one asks why.
You carried it until your wrists ached. Your shoulders grew a step stronger.
There were a few useful things left in the house. If you stay too long, the ceiling will collapse.
You watched until the district completely sank. Only dust remained in your eyes.
낯익은 그림자가 당신 앞을 막는다. 오래전 도운 이거나 오래전 외면한 이: A familiar shadow blocks your path. It is someone you helped long ago, or someone you turned away long ago. The shadow speaks: they have come to settle the score.
빚이 있다면 갚는다: Pay the debt if you owe one
The shadow nodded. As the price was paid, your body felt lighter.
The shadow laughed. In this City, saying you have no debt is the oldest joke.
The shadow passed by. The settlement was postponed.
경비가 교대하는 시간이다. 모든 골목에서 한꺼번에 발소리가 멈춘다. 이: It is time for the guards to change shifts. Footsteps stop in every alley all at once. This City breathes in a steady rhythm.
You went the furthest during this short gap. No one saw you.
All the guards looked like they had the same face. You shouldn't make eye contact for too long.
Waiting is also a job. In this City, they call it a break.
손가락의 연락책이 새 지령서를 내민다. 지령서의 끝은 비어 있다. 끝이: A contact from the Fingers hands you a new directive. The end of the directive is blank. They say there are no more directives with an end.
첫 줄을 읽자마자 몸이 알아서 움직였다. 이 일에는 이름이 없고 값만 있: As soon as you read the first line, your body moved on its own. This job has no name, only a price.
The contact stood there and waited. Their expression suggested that refusal was also part of the directive.
지령서의 빈 곳에 내 답을 적는다: Write your answer in the blank space of the directive
당신이 적은 글이 지령서 아래로 스며들었다. 다음 지령부터는 문체가 달라: The words you wrote seeped into the directive. From the next directive on, the writing style had changed.
어디선가 낮은 소리가 들린다. 말은 아닌데 뜻은 안다. 도시가 한 번 숨: A low sound is heard from somewhere. It is not speech, but you understand the meaning. It is the sound of the City catching its breath.
소리 안에 당신의 이름이 있었다. 부르는 것인지 세는 것인지는 알 수 없: Your name was within the sound. You cannot tell if it is calling you or counting you.
Even after the sound stopped, your hand did not leave your ear for a long time.
The sound circled a district and returned to where it started. In the meantime, your feet became lighter.
젊은 해결사가 당신에게 묻는다. 이렇게 오래 사는 법이 뭡니까. 대답하기: A young Fixer asks you: How do you live so long? Before you can answer, his eyes are fixed on the tip of your blade.
Most of what you said was a lie. Still, that Fixer lived a long time.
It was an honest answer. The Fixer turned away with a disappointed look.
칼을 쥐고 겨뤄 보자고 한다: Draw your blade and suggest a spar
가르치는 것과 시험하는 것은 같은 일이다. 몇 합 뒤 해결사가 먼저 고개: Teaching and testing are the same thing. After a few exchanges, the Fixer was the first to bow his head.
The Fixer's blade grazed you. You saw his lips move to apologize first.
It is the day to organize the documents that have piled up over a long time. Each document is a year. As you read, some years are left with only a name.
The ashes flew away lightly. Your body remembers only what it needs to remember.
You read for a long time. There were many things that were never written down.
The number of names you set aside was unexpectedly small. That is why you look at them for longer.
골목 의자에 늙은 해결사가 앉아 있다. 오래된 칼은 무릎 위에 올려 두고: An old Fixer sits on a chair in the alley. He has an old blade resting on his knees. When your eyes meet, he nods. In this City, it is a signal recognized by those who have paid the same price.
There were not many words. You looked in the same direction until the sun set.
늙은 해결사는 칼을 내밀었다. 칼날에 새겨진 숫자는 당신의 연차보다 많았: The old Fixer held out his blade. The numbers engraved on the blade were greater than your years of experience.
It was the most appropriate greeting for each other.
의뢰서의 머리말은 마지막이라고 적혀 있다. 이 도시에서 마지막은 다음 의: The header of the request says it is the final one. In this City, "final" only means "until the next request arrives."
마지막이라는 말은 값을 올려 받는 데 쓰였다. 일은 쉽지 않았지만 끝은: The word "final" was used to drive up the price. The job wasn't easy, but the ending was clean.
The folded request had been in the drawer for a long time. The next request arrived right on time.
의뢰인은 이미 자리에 없었다. 책상 위에는 마지막이 아닌 의뢰서만 쌓여: The client was already gone. On the desk, only requests that weren't the "final" one were piled up.
지도 한 장을 펼쳤더니 낯선 구역이 그려져 있다. 지도에 없던 길이 생겼: I unfolded a map to find an unfamiliar area drawn on it. They say a path that wasn't on the map has appeared. No, it’s that an erased path has been revived.
I found an old well where the map pointed. The water was clear.
Every path on the map is more unfamiliar than the one I am walking now.
The line you drew changed the City by one stroke. You decided to believe that.
계절이 바뀌는 것을 알려 주는 건 이 도시에서 혈흔 색깔이다. 올해는 짙: In this City, it is the color of bloodstains that tells us the seasons are changing. This year, it's on the darker side.
My hands were scrubbed for a long time. In the process, my hands felt lighter.
Footprints were left clearly behind. The one chasing me will be pleased.
Waiting until the color changes is also a method.
쓰러진 괴수에게서 떨어진 조각 하나가 아직 희미하게 맥박친다. 쥐면 따뜻: A fragment that fell from the fallen monster still pulses faintly. It is warm when held, and vanishes when let go.
The fragment embedded itself into my hand. It didn't hurt. A few days later, the wound was gone.
The fragment shattered without a sound. My ears felt muffled for a moment.
The collector gave the fragment a name. The price was determined by that name.
광장에 전광판이 켜져 있다. 올해의 위협 등급이 한 줄씩 지나간다. 맨: The display board in the plaza is lit. This year's threat levels scroll by line by line. Your name flickers on the bottom line.
After watching for a while, the name disappeared. The vanished name will appear somewhere else.
The plaza went quiet. The quiet plaza felt even noisier.
이름 아래에 적힌 숫자를 읽는다: Read the number written under the name
Your number was still rising. There is no end to the rising number.
부서진 구역이 다시 올라간다. 사람들은 벽돌을 나른다. 이 도시는 늘 부: The destroyed district is being rebuilt. People carry bricks. This City is always being destroyed and always being rebuilt.
I carried them until my shoulders burned. It was a long day.
One wall was raised with your money. No name was left behind.
I stood for a long time watching the wall go up.
가게 구석에 오래된 거울이 걸려 있다. 비친 얼굴은 당신이 기억하는 것보: An old mirror hangs in the corner of the shop. The face reflected is a bit more unfamiliar than the one you remember. Still, the eyes are the same.
거울 속 눈이 먼저 시선을 거두었다. 이 도시에서 오래 산다는 것은 그런: The eyes in the mirror looked away first. That is what it means to live a long time in this City.
Beneath the dust, an even older face appeared. That face, too, was one I knew.
거울을 등지고 걷는다: Turn your back to the mirror and walk
The mirror shook once behind my back.
가족 식사 · 상석: Family meal · Head of the table
큰 상의 맨 안쪽 자리가 비어 있다. 모두가 당신이 앉기를 기다린다. 형: The seat at the very end of the large table is empty. Everyone is waiting for you to sit. The elders have raised their glasses, and the youngest cannot lift their heads.
상석에 앉는다: Sit at the head of the table
당신이 잔을 들자 상이 한꺼번에 움직였다. 자리에는 무게가 있었고, 그: As you raised your glass, the table moved in unison. The seat had a weight to it, and that weight settled onto your shoulders.
One of the youngest dropped their spoon. You pretended not to notice and picked up the same side dish. The head of the table remained empty, but the meal that day stayed warm longer than usual.
집의 빈 방: The empty room in the house
집에 방이 하나 늘어 있다. 지은 적 없는 방인데 {배우자}의 물건이 가: There is an extra room in the house. It’s a room I never built, yet {배우자}'s belongings are neatly arranged inside. When I asked {배우자}, they said the room was there from the beginning. It is strange that the words don't sound like a lie.
의자 하나가 놓여 있었다. 앉으니 오래 쓴 몸에 꼭 맞았다. 문틈으로 {: A chair was placed there. Sitting in it, it fit my long-worn body perfectly. Through the crack in the door, {배우자}'s voice reached me a beat late.
쓸 만한 것을 몇 개 챙겼다. {배우자}는 아무 말 없이 방문을 닫아 주: I took a few useful things. {배우자} closed the door without a word.
불꽃은 크지 않았다. 이 자리에서는 지우는 것이 남기는 것보다 오래 간다: The flames were not large. In this place, erasing something lasts longer than leaving it behind. {배우자} watched the flames for a long time.
집에 방이 하나 늘어 있다. 지은 적 없는 방이다. 안에는 먼저 떠난 {: There is an extra room in the house. It’s a room I never built. Inside, the belongings of the departed {배우자} remain exactly as they were. It seems someone has been cleaning it continuously.
의자 하나가 놓여 있었다. 앉으니 오래 쓴 몸에 꼭 맞았다. 어디선가 {: A chair was placed there. Sitting in it, it fit my long-worn body perfectly. It felt as if {배우자}'s name had been called from somewhere.
I took a few useful things. My hand was a bit slow to close the door as I left.
불꽃은 크지 않았다. 이 자리에서는 지우는 것이 남기는 것보다 오래 간다: The flames were not large. In this place, erasing something lasts longer than leaving it behind.
집에 방이 하나 늘어 있다. 지은 적 없는 방인데 문은 열려 있고 안은: There is an extra room in the house. It’s a room I never built, but the door is open and the inside is tidy. It seems someone has been cleaning it continuously.
A chair was placed there. Sitting in it, it fit my long-worn body perfectly.
집 앞길에서 아이들이 뛰어논다. 그중 한 아이가 {손주}이라는 이름으로: Children are playing on the street in front of the house. One of them is called by the name {손주}. They resemble {아이}'s child. Even though there is no reason for a child to be here, the child knows your face.
The child approached without shyness and reached out a hand. Their fingertips were warm.
The child was still looking back from the same spot even after a long time.
아이는 자기 이름이 불린 것보다 당신 목소리에 놀란 얼굴이었다. 우연이라: The child looked more surprised by your voice than by their name being called. I decided to consider it a coincidence.
Children are playing on the street in front of the house. Among them is a face that resembles {아이}. Even though {아이} is already fully grown, the same face runs with the same gait. The child in this place does not seem to grow.
아이가 말한 이름은 당신이 오래전 알던 이름이었다. 우연이라고 생각하기로: The name the child spoke was one I had known a long time ago. I decided to consider it a coincidence.
집 앞길에서 아이들이 뛰어논다. 이 자리에 아이가 있을 리 없는데, 그중: Children are playing on the street in front of the house. There is no reason for a child to be here, but one of them looks at you as if they recognize you. Their eyes resemble someone's.
집 담장 아래에 이름 없는 아이가 앉아 있다. {아이}의 어릴 적 얼굴과: A nameless child is sitting under the house wall. Their face resembles {아이}'s childhood face, but even {아이} says they don't know this child. It is not rare for someone to be nameless in this place. However, this child knows that they have no name.
아이는 이름을 몇 번 소리 내어 읽었다. 그 소리가 당신을 한 번 돌아보: The child read the name aloud a few times. The sound made you look back once.
The child did not take their eyes off the food. Only after you left did they reach out.
I have become accustomed to passing by nameless existences.
집 담장 아래에 이름 없는 아이가 앉아 있다. 이름이 없는 건 이 자리에: A nameless child is sitting under the house wall. Being nameless is not rare in this place. However, this child knows that they have no name.
어제 없던 계단: The stairs that weren't there yesterday
집 뒤편에 계단이 하나 늘어 있다. 어디로도 이어지지 않는데 오르는 발소: There is an extra staircase behind the house. It leads nowhere, yet the sound of footsteps climbing is clearly heard from above. The stairs weren't there until yesterday. No, it’s that I have no memory of them being there until yesterday.
Looking from one step up, the house looked a span lower. When I came down, the stairs were gone.
아래에는 그림자만 쌓여 있었다. 그림자는 당신 것이 아니었다. 가져가도: Only shadows were piled up underneath. The shadows were not yours. Not knowing if I should take them, I left them there.
보지 않은 척 지나간다: Pretend not to see and pass by
보지 않는 사이 계단이 한 칸 늘었다. 그렇게 이 자리는 조금씩 어긋난다: The stairs grew by one step while I wasn't looking. This place shifts, little by little.
같은 길을 한참 걸었다. 이정표의 숫자는 줄지 않는다. 걸은 만큼 길이: I walked the same path for a long time. The numbers on the signpost never decrease. It feels as if the path grows as much as I walk. Here, the near is far, and the far is near.
한 걸음마다 숫자가 한 칸씩 올라갔다. 어느 순간부터 걷는 일이 호흡처럼: The number increased by one with every step. At some point, walking became as natural as breathing.
A house stood where I turned around. It looked as if it had been there from the start.
The signpost came out easily. The numbers vanished the moment I pulled it.
해가 지는데 그림자가 두 개다. 하나는 발치에 붙어 있고, 하나는 반 걸: The sun is setting, yet there are two shadows. One is attached to my feet, and the other is half a step away. Both resemble me. I cannot tell which one arrived here first.
그림자는 같은 속도로 물러났다. 둘 사이의 거리가 당신이 이 자리에 머문: The shadow retreated at the same speed. The distance between the two was equal to the number of years I had stayed in this place.
발치의 그림자를 밟는다: Step on the shadow at my feet
The shadow did not get stepped on; it simply lowered itself. My body felt a little lighter.
해가 지기를 기다린다: Wait for the sun to set
해가 지자 그림자는 하나만 남았다. 어느 쪽이 남았는지 묻지 않기로 했다: When the sun set, only one shadow remained. I decided not to ask which one it was.
문 앞의 신발: Shoes in Front of the Door
문 앞에 신발 한 켤레가 놓여 있다. 당신 것은 아닌데 크기가 꼭 맞는다: A pair of shoes sits in front of the door. They aren't mine, but they fit perfectly. There are no signs of wear, yet the soles are wet as if they had just been walked in.
신발은 걷는 방향을 먼저 알고 있었다. 한참 걸었는데 집 앞으로 돌아와: The shoes already knew the way. I walked for a long time, only to end up back in front of the house.
현관에 놓았더니 신발은 조금 낮아졌다. 이 집의 식구가 하나 늘어난 기분: When I placed them in the entryway, the shoes seemed to settle. It feels as if the house has gained a new member.
버린 신발은 밤 사이 문 앞으로 돌아와 있었다. 이번에는 한 켤레가 아니: The discarded shoes were back in front of the door by nightfall. This time, there was more than one pair.
{배우자}가 오늘은 어제보다 조금 어려 보인다. 아니, 조금 늙어 보인다: {배우자} looks a bit younger today than yesterday. No, a bit older. It changes every time I look. Here, time seems to flow in layers over a person's face.
{배우자} answered as always. The response arrived a beat late.
The hand was warm. The warmth itself felt unbelievable.
Later, I noticed {배우자} had also been staring at my face for a long time.
복도에서 발소리가 난다. 먼저 떠난 {배우자}의 걸음이다. 문을 열면 아: There are footsteps in the hallway. They are the steps of {배우자}, who left long ago. I know that if I open the door, no one will be there. Still, the footsteps are one step closer than they were yesterday.
There was no one in the hallway. Instead, warmth remained on the floor.
There was no answer. Instead, a door closed somewhere in the house.
발소리는 멈추지 않았다. 멈추지 않는 것에 익숙해지는 것이 이 자리에서: The footsteps did not stop. Getting used to things that never stop is how one lives in this place.
집으로 가는 길 끝에 가로등이 한 줄로 서 있다. 불은 땅 쪽으로 켜져: Streetlights stand in a row at the end of the path to the house. The lights shine toward the ground, and the shadows lie toward the sky. Here, the light is visible not when you look up, but when you look down.
바닥에 비친 빛 속에서 몸의 윤곽이 잠깐 또렷해졌다. 숨을 고르자 몸이: My silhouette became clear for a moment within the light reflected on the ground. As I caught my breath, my body felt light.
가로등을 뽑아 본다: Try to pull out a streetlight
뽑히지는 않았다. 대신 손바닥에 빛의 결이 남았다. 칼이 조금 더 선명하: It wouldn't budge. Instead, a trace of light remained on my palm. My blade feels a bit sharper.
Only after passing did I realize the light had been off.
비가 내린다. 옷은 젖지 않고 땅도 마르다. 소리만 크게 들린다. 이 자: It is raining. My clothes are not wet, and the ground is dry. Only the sound is loud. Here, even the rain falls and stops at set times, as if it were just doing its job.
비가 그친 순간 몸이 한 번 떨렸다. 어디선가 오래 쌓였던 것이 빠져나갔: The moment the rain stopped, my body shuddered. Something that had been piling up for a long time drained away.
비 소리를 센다: Count the sound of the rain
한 방울마다 숫자 하나가 떠올랐다. 어느 숫자에서 멈추는지 기억해 두었다: A number surfaced with every drop. I memorized the number where it stopped.
When the door closed, the sound of the rain cut off a beat late.
길가에 이정표가 반쯤 땅에 묻혀 있다. 도시까지 몇 걸음인지 적혀 있지만: A signpost is half-buried in the ground by the roadside. It says how many steps it is to the City, but the number changes every time I read it. Here, it is not the distance that changes, but the reader.
I didn't remember the number the next day. Only the fact that I had memorized it remained in my body.
세운 이정표는 처음부터 서 있었다는 얼굴이었다. 돌아오는 길이 조금 편해: The reset signpost looked as if it had been standing there all along. The walk back felt a little easier.
When I looked back, the signpost had sunk even deeper.
개울 위에 다리가 놓여 있다. 가운데가 끊어져 있는데 건너편에서 사람이: A bridge spans the stream. The middle is broken, yet someone is waving from the other side. I don't know how to cross, but the other side is clearly close.
뛰는 순간 다리가 한 칸 이어졌다. 건너편에는 아무도 없었고 손짓만 남아: The moment I jumped, the bridge connected for a split second. There was no one on the other side, only the lingering gesture.
The person who received the answer seemed to smile. The bridge remains broken in its place.
The water does not flow, but the sound does. After sitting for a while, my body relaxed.
빈터에 시계 가게가 서 있다. 진열된 시계들은 모두 같은 시각에서 멈춰: A clock shop stands in a vacant lot. All the clocks on display are stopped at the same time, but mine is still ticking. The owner watches only my wrist from the darkness inside.
돌려받은 시계는 한 바퀴 느리게 가고 있었다. 하루가 조금 길어진 기분이: The watch I got back was running one lap slow. It feels as if the day has grown a little longer.
가게 시계를 사 본다: Buy a clock from the shop
The clock I bought stopped as soon as I unwrapped it. Even a stopped clock has its price here.
As soon as I stepped out, the clock chimed loudly once. The shop was already gone.
잎만 있고 가지가 없는 나무가 서 있다. 줄기에 귀를 대면 바람 소리가: A tree with leaves but no branches stands there. If you press your ear to the trunk, you can hear the sound of wind. They say the trees here have no need to grow branches because their only job is to stand.
바람 소리 안에 오래 전에 들은 목소리가 섞여 있었다. 누구인지는 끝내: A voice I heard long ago was mixed into the sound of the wind. I could never tell whose it was.
The tree supported my weight. I understood why they said their only job was to stand.
돌아본 자리에 잎이 한 장 떨어져 있었다. 가지가 없는데 어디서 떨어진: A leaf had fallen where I looked back. There are no branches, so where could it have fallen from?
처마에 풍경이 걸려 있다. 바람이 없는데 소리가 난다. 소리는 같은 간격: A wind chime hangs from the eaves. There is no wind, yet it makes a sound. The sound rings at regular intervals, and the intervals are narrowing little by little. It feels like a signal that something is approaching.
The detached wind chime stopped making sound. Instead, the same sound rang inside my ears.
소리는 걷는 속도에 맞춰 느려지고 빨라졌다. 어느 순간 걷는 것이 가볍게: The sound slowed down and sped up in time with my walking. At some point, walking became effortless.
When I pretended not to hear it, the sound pretended not to exist. We got along well.
우물가의 물에 집이 비친다. 비친 집은 지금 서 있는 집보다 조금 크고: The house is reflected in the well water. The reflected house is slightly larger than the one I am standing in, and the lights are on. I cannot see who is standing by the window. I only know for sure that it is not me.
The water was not cold. The sensation of a doorknob remained on my hand when I pulled it out.
When I threw a stone, the house shattered. A single fragment ended up in my pocket.
I heard a window close behind me as I turned away.
집 울타리 너머에 또 다른 울타리가 있다. 그 너머에도 있다. 세어 보면: There is another fence beyond the house's fence. And another beyond that. If I count them, there are always seven layers, but none of them are fences I haven't seen before. Here, the inside is the most unfamiliar.
한 바퀴를 돌자 집 앞이었다. 일곱 겹의 울타리는 어디에서도 이어지지 않: After one lap, I was back in front of the house. The seven-layered fence did not connect anywhere.
The same fence stood where I had climbed over. My body felt a little more tempered.
Only the repaired spot looked new, catching my eye for a long time.
집 앞마당에 발자국이 나 있다. 크기도 걸음의 폭도 당신 것이다. 문 앞: There are footprints in the front yard. The size and stride are yours. They end at the door, and there are no footprints inside. Who could have just entered?
발자국은 걷는 대로 따라 생겼다. 나란히 걷던 걸음이 어느새 하나로 겹쳤: The footprints appeared as I walked. The steps I took alongside them soon overlapped into one.
쓸어 낸 자리에 같은 발자국이 다시 생기지는 않았다. 마당이 한결 조용해: The same footprints did not reappear where I swept. The yard became much quieter.
The inside of the house was as usual. Only the chair was warm, as if someone had just sat up from it.
한 장 늘어난 달력: A calendar with an extra page.
벽의 달력이 한 장 늘어 있다. 맨 뒤 장은 아직 써지지 않은 달인데 날: There is one extra page on the wall calendar. The last page is for a date not yet written, but each date box has a small mark. It is a sign that someone has lived through each day in advance.
The next page was empty. Being empty actually put my mind at ease.
표시 하나에 날짜를 적는다: Write the date on a mark.
The box with the written date flickered once. My body grew stronger by the day's share.
It was the same side even when flipped. There is no back side to this place.
마당의 빨랫줄에 옷이 걸려 있다. 몇 해째 마르지 않았다. 물방울이 떨어: Clothes are hanging on the clothesline in the yard. They haven't dried for years. The sound of water droplets falling can be heard, but the ground doesn't get wet. I no longer remember who the clothes belong to.
걷어서 개킨다: Take them down and fold them.
갠 옷은 처음부터 개켜 있던 것처럼 가지런했다. 정리한 만큼 마음이 가라: The folded clothes were as neat as if they had been folded from the start. My mind settled as much as I tidied up.
They smelled of something I had smelled long ago. I couldn't recall where.
The same sound of water droplets occurred the next day. This sound became a part of the house.
아침 해가 떴는데 그림자가 하나도 없다. 집도, 나무도, 당신도. 모든: The morning sun has risen, but there are no shadows. Not the house, not the trees, not you. Everything is laid out like a flat picture. In this place, even shadows sometimes take a day off.
저녁이 되자 그림자가 한꺼번에 돌아왔다. 한 박 늦게 도착한 그림자가 몸: When evening came, the shadows returned all at once. The shadow that arrived a beat late fit my body perfectly.
The landscape grew a layer thicker with every step. My senses became clearer with each stride.
집 안에는 평소처럼 그림자가 있었다. 집이 이 자리에서 가장 믿을 만한: There were shadows inside the house as usual. The house is the most reliable place to be.
집 앞에서 한 사람이 소리를 판다. 병에 담긴 웃음소리, 문 닫는 소리,: A person sells sounds in front of the house. Laughter in a bottle, the sound of a closing door, the sound of a name being called long ago. They say the price is paid with what the buyer remembers longest.
이름을 부르는 소리를 산다: Buy the sound of a name being called.
병을 열자 목소리가 한 번 울렸다. 값으로 내어 준 기억은 무엇인지 알: When I opened the bottle, the voice rang out once. I could not tell what memory I had given as payment.
The laughter echoed inside my body for a long time. For the first time in a while, I breathed easily.
그 사람은 인사도 없이 사라졌다. 빈자리에 병 하나가 놓여 있었다. 비어: The person disappeared without a word of farewell. A bottle was left in their place. It is empty.
문턱이 조금 낮아졌다. 지난달에는 발을 올려야 넘던 문턱이다. 집이 당신: The threshold has lowered a little. Last month, I had to lift my feet to cross it. It doesn't seem strange to think the house is growing to match your height. Yet, the threshold is lower than yesterday, and higher than today.
The threshold was the perfect height for sitting. After sitting for a while, my body felt at ease.
The line I drew was a palm's width higher the next day. The house grows little by little.
모른 척 넘는다: Cross it while pretending not to notice.
The moment I crossed, the light inside the house flickered once.
부엌에서 음식 냄새가 난다. 끓이지 않았는데 솥은 따뜻하다. 어디서 배운: There is a smell of food in the kitchen. The pot is warm even though nothing is boiling. A bowl of soup, the flavor of which I don't recognize, is set out. Eating it feels like becoming a member of this house.
The soup tasted like something I had eaten long ago. After eating, I wasn't hungry for a while.
The pot was empty. Steam rose from the empty pot.
When I turned off the heat, the smell vanished as well. The house seemed a little sad.
The backyard is widening step by step. The fence I could reach last year is now far away. I don't know if the house is eating the land or if the land is expanding the house. Either way, this house is becoming the largest presence in this place.
마당을 걸어 넓이를 잰다: Walk the yard to measure its width.
The number of steps taken in one lap was higher than yesterday. My breathing deepened as I walked.
씨를 뿌린 자리에 싹이 하루 만에 올랐다. 먹을 수 있는 것인지는 모르겠: Sprouts appeared in the spot where I sowed seeds after only one day. I don't know if they are edible.
The rebuilt fence stood one step inward the next day.
지붕 위에서 발소리가 난다. 올라가 보니 아무도 없는데 기와 한 장이 따: There are footsteps on the roof. When I went up, there was no one there, but a roof tile was warm. It seems a guest had already come and rested. This house does not turn anyone away.
A name was written on the back. It was a name I had never seen before, but it was easy to call.
The tea I left was empty by nightfall. The house became much gentler.
The same tile was warm the next day as well.
집 안의 물건들이 당신보다 먼저 자리를 바꾸어 놓는다. 컵은 늘 오른손: The objects in the house change their positions before you do. The cup is always on the right, the chair by the window. This house knows you have lived here for a long time better than you do.
집이 놓아 둔 대로 움직이자 하루가 매끄러웠다. 몸이 집에 맞춰 단단해졌: Moving as the house placed things made the day smooth. My body grew firm in tune with the house.
일부러 어긋나게 놓는다: Deliberately place things out of order.
어긋나게 놓은 컵이 밤사이 제자리에 와 있었다. 집이 한 번 웃은 것 같: The cup I placed out of order was back in its place by nightfall. It felt as if the house had laughed once.
There was no answer. Only the porch light flickered twice.
창밖에 도시가 보인다. 불빛이 켜진 건물들, 오가는 사람들. 손을 뻗으면: The City is visible outside the window. Buildings with lights on, people coming and going. It feels like I could reach it if I stretched out my hand, but opening the window always reveals the same vacant lot. Only from this house can I see the City.
창가에 오래 선다: Stand by the window for a long time.
도시의 소리가 먼 곳에서 들렸다. 돌아갈 곳이 있다는 느낌이 몸을 단단하: The sounds of the City were heard from afar. The feeling that there was a place to return to made my body firm.
Beyond the open window was a vacant lot. A breeze blew once, and the scent of the City drifted in.
The City stood for a long time behind the curtains. It is there even if I don't look.
현관에 이름표가 붙어 있다. 이름 칸이 비어 있다가 오늘은 잉크가 번져: There is a nameplate on the porch. The name field was empty, but today the ink is smudged. When I try to read it, the letters take shape a beat late. This house has not yet decided on a name.
적은 이름은 현관에서 한 번 빛나고 사라졌다. 그날의 집이 유난히 따뜻했: The written name shone once on the porch and vanished. The house was exceptionally warm that day.
On the back was a name erased long ago. I flipped it back without reading it.
The nameplate was empty again after one day. Even if it is empty, the house is still a house.
집 바닥 밑에서 무언가 숨 쉬는 소리가 난다. 기둥을 두드리면 한 박 늦: There is a sound of something breathing beneath the floor of the house. If I knock on the pillar, the knocking returns a beat late. Perhaps this house is not standing on the ground, but embedded within it.
바닥에 귀를 댄다: Press your ear to the floor
The breathing was slow and deep. As you steadied your breath to match that rhythm, your body grew quiet.
The tapping returned three times. It felt like a signal that the house acknowledged you.
The sound stopped for a while under the rug. The silence was more unsettling.
집 문 아래로 의뢰서가 한 장 밀려 들어와 있다. 의뢰인의 이름도, 보수: A request has been slid under the door. There is no client name, no reward, only a location. It is strangely comforting that even here, there are people looking for a Fixer.
의뢰는 누구도 다치지 않고 끝났다. 끝난 것도 이상한 일이었다. 보수는: The request ended without anyone getting hurt. It was strange that it ended at all. The reward was left at the door.
의뢰서를 접어 서랍에 넣는다: Fold the request and put it in the drawer
The drawer was filled with several identical requests. Only the locations were different.
They never came. The day spent waiting allowed your body to rest.
서랍 깊숙한 곳에서 낡은 급수 배지가 나온다. 어느 급이었는지 이제는 읽: An old Grade badge is found deep in the drawer. It is no longer legible which grade it was. In this place, a Fixer is not defined by their grade, but by the fact that they are still standing.
배지를 가슴에 단다: Pin the badge to your chest
The badge sat on your chest with an aged weight. After pinning it on, your posture straightened slightly.
The polished badge reflected your face like a mirror. It had been a long time since you saw your own face.
As you closed the drawer, the badge rang once. It was the sound of someone remembering you from afar.
협회의 마지막 서류: The last document from the Association
협회에서 서류가 한 통 왔다. 어느 건물에서 보냈는지, 이 자리까지 어떻: A document arrived from the Association. No one knows which building sent it or how it reached this place. There is no date written on it. In this place, Association documents are the only record that tells you what day it is.
The document vanished the moment you signed it. Only your name remained with the Association. You felt a little more secure.
읽는 동안 글자가 한 줄씩 늘었다. 끝까지 읽으면 오래 살게 되는 문서: While reading, the text grew by a line. It felt like a document that would grant a long life if read to the end.
The ashes floated in the shape of letters for a moment before settling.
날개의 낡은 깃: An old feather from a Wing
집 문틈에 낡은 깃이 끼어 있다. 소속 날개의 문장이 새겨져 있다. 날개: An old feather is caught in the door crack. The crest of a Wing is engraved on it. A Wing is a place that cannot reach this location, yet the feather arrived first. The sender is nowhere to be seen.
The feather grew warm the moment you grasped it. The sensation of belonging to an organization for a long time returned to your arm.
깃을 창가에 꽂아 둔다: Place the feather on the windowsill
창가의 깃은 바람이 없는데 흔들렸다. 날개가 멀리서 안부를 묻는 것 같다: The feather on the windowsill swayed despite the lack of wind. It felt as if the Wing was asking after you from afar.
When you returned the feather to the door crack, it was gone by the next day.
서열이 있는 곳의 사람이 집 앞에서 서서 인사만 하고 간다. 일을 시키러: Someone from a place with a hierarchy stands before the house, offers a greeting, and leaves. They say they didn't come to assign work, but to ask how you are. In this place, hierarchy remains as a greeting.
답을 들은 사람은 고개를 숙이고 갔다. 몸이 조직의 박에 오랜만에 맞았다: The person who heard your reply bowed their head and left. For the first time in a while, your body matched the rhythm of an organization.
A small bundle was left where they had sat to drink tea.
문 너머에서 한참 기다리는 기척이 났다. 기척이 사라질 때까지 문을 열지: There was a presence waiting for a long time on the other side of the door. You did not open it until the presence vanished.
사무소 인장이 우편함에 들어 있다. 이름 칸이 비어 있는 인장이다. 이: A workshop seal is in the mailbox. It is a seal with an empty space for a name. In this place, workshop work means receiving no work from anyone. Still, the seal looks for a place to be pressed.
The name of the workshop appeared where you stamped it. It was not work that was prepared, but a place.
인장을 서랍에 넣는다: Put the seal in the drawer
인장은 서랍 속에서 한 번 눌린 소리를 냈다. 일이 하나 처리된 것 같다: The seal made a sound as if it had been pressed once inside the drawer. It felt like a task had been processed.
인장을 문에 걸어 둔다: Hang the seal on the door
The seal hanging on the door swayed without wind. Those who come and go will recognize it.
엄지에서 오래 지키던 약속이 이 자리까지 따라왔다. 약속은 형태가 없고: A promise long kept by the Thumb has followed you to this place. The promise has no form, only weight. In this place, a promise does not vanish even if it is not kept.
The renewed promise pulsed like a heartbeat within your body. Your body grew firmer with its weight.
The released promise swayed once and then settled. Your shoulders felt lighter.
The promise you kept was warm. It is the only warm thing in this place.
검지에서 오던 지령이 끊어진 지 오래인데 오늘은 한 장이 도착했다. 글씨: It has been a long time since the directives from the Index stopped, but one arrived today. The handwriting is familiar, but the content changes every time you read it. It seems the ones issuing the directives are also experiencing the displacement of this place.
따른 지령은 끝나기도 전에 다음 지령으로 이어졌다. 몸이 알아서 움직이게: The directive you followed led to the next one before it even ended. Your body began to move on its own.
고친 글자가 한 줄 남고 나머지는 사라졌다. 이 자리에서 지령은 합의가: One line of the corrected text remained, and the rest vanished. In this place, a directive becomes an agreement.
The unread directive grew old on the windowsill. The older it got, the softer it became.
문고리에 사슬이 감겨 있다. 중지의 사슬이다. 끊으려 하면 풀리고 풀려: A chain is wrapped around the door handle. It is a chain of the Middle. If you try to break it, it loosens; if you try to loosen it, it tightens. What cannot be let go of even in this place is the act of not letting go of each other.
The chain grew quiet while wrapped around your arm. The weight pressed down on your body, making you stand all the straighter.
The released chain made a sound on the ground once and vanished. The spot where it disappeared was warm.
문고리째 둔다: Leave it on the door handle
The chain rang slightly every time you opened the door. After a long time, it sounded like a clock.
약지에서 맞춘 반지가 서랍에서 나왔다. 어느 쪽 손가락에도 맞지 않는데: A ring tailored by the Ring appeared in the drawer. It doesn't fit any finger, but when you put it on, it fits. In this place, "fitting" is not a matter of shape, but of the time you have held onto it.
The moment you put it on, the ring clung to your finger. It soaked into your body like a long-worn garment.
반지를 창가에 둔다: Place the ring on the windowsill
The ring on the windowsill sparkled once every time the sun set.
There was no one to hand it to. The mere gesture of trying to hand it over made your heart quiet.
집 앞길 끝에 공방 주인이 와 있다. 도시의 거리에서 가게를 열던 사람이: The workshop owner is standing at the end of the path in front of the house. They are someone who used to run a shop on the streets of the City. They say they dragged their luggage all the way here. Not because there were no customers left in the City, but because they needed a customer who has been standing in this place for a long time.
가게를 연다고 한다: Say you will open the shop
The owner set up a workbench by the roadside. A shop in this place stands only as much as it is needed. That shop appears when you visit the workshop district.
The luggage was light, but it felt heavy when you set it down. The owner bowed their head.
The owner looked back once and walked to the end of the path. The shop stood at the end of the road.
해결사 등록도 소속도 없는 사람이 집 앞에 서 있다. 같은 이름도, 같은: A person with no Fixer registration and no affiliation is standing in front of the house. They are not of the same name or the same path, yet they have come to this place in the same way. Both of you know that you are losing your names in this place.
차를 마신 사람이 입을 열었다. 이 자리에 온 이유를 이야기하는 동안 몸: The person who drank the tea opened their mouth. As they spoke of the reason they came to this place, your body relaxed.
Your steps were in sync. When you walked to the end of the path and returned, your body felt a little firmer.
There was a presence standing outside the door for a long time. When the sun set, the presence vanished.
적중 시 못을 모두 흐트러짐으로 (1:1): On hit, turn all Nails into Stagger (1:1)
장부를 든 수금원이 앞을 막는다. 이 구역의 상납금은 아직 덜 걷혔다고: A collector holding a ledger blocks the way. They say the tribute for this district hasn't been fully collected yet.
같은 가문의 다른 후보가 길을 막는다. 흑수환으로 쥐의 특성을 지닌 흑수: Another candidate from the same family blocks the path. They are accompanied by a subordinate—a Kurokumo Clan member with rat-like traits. The ox's bit belongs to the head of the family, so this candidate does not have it. With one seat at stake, the two do not call each other brother.
The silence connected us. In this place, silence is the most solid thing.
이야기를 끝까지 듣는다: Listen to the story to the end
While listening, something I had forgotten surfaced. What I recalled rested upon the tip of my blade.
In the silence, our breathing fell into the same rhythm.
The bedding smelled like the child. After sitting for a while, my body relaxed.
정리한 방은 하루 만에 원래 모습으로 돌아와 있었다. 집이 아이의 자리를: The room returned to its original state after a single day. It seems the house protects the child's place.
The sound of the child's footsteps echoed once from beyond the door. I did not check.
쓴 답장은 현관에 놓자 사라졌다. 어디로 갔는지는 모르지만 도착한 것 같: The reply I wrote vanished once placed in the entryway. I do not know where it went, but it felt as though it had arrived.
편지를 가슴에 품는다: Hold the letter to my chest
The letter was warm. That warmth wrapped around my body for the day.
편지를 서랍에 넣는다: Put the letter in the drawer
서랍에는 같은 편지가 여러 장 있었다. 한 번도 열지 않은 것이 아니었다: There were several identical letters in the drawer. It was not as if I had never opened them.
The small hand was warm. When I let go, warmth remained on my palm.
이름을 부르자 아이는 처음 듣는 듯 웃었다. 그 웃음이 하루 종일 집에: When I called their name, the child smiled as if hearing it for the first time. That smile remained in the house all day.
아이는 받은 과자를 호주머니에 넣고 사라졌다. 호주머니는 비어 있었을 것: The child put the snack in their pocket and vanished. The pocket must have been empty.
의자를 창가로 옮긴다: Move the chair to the window
창가의 의자는 해가 질 때마다 한 번 비스듬히 기울었다. 누군가 앉았다: The chair by the window tilted slightly every time the sun set. It felt as if someone had sat down and stood up.
I placed a cup of tea in front of the chair left as is. The tea was empty by morning.
휴게실에서 갓 등록한 해결사가 머뭇거리며 말을 건다. 특색에 닿은 사람의: A newly registered Fixer hesitates in the lounge and speaks to me. They ask to see the fight of someone who has touched a Color just once.
칼을 뽑지 않고도 어디를 막아야 하는지만 보여 주었다. 후배는 오래 고개: I showed them where to block without even drawing my blade. The junior bowed their head for a long time. The act of teaching remained in my body as well.
말은 짧았다. 후배는 그 말을 받아 적었다. 적어 가는 손이 서툴렀지만: My words were brief. The junior wrote them down. Their hand was clumsy, but they did not make a mistake.
오래된 단골이 작업대 앞에 선다. 사업을 넓히는 중이라 칼과 방패를 한꺼: A long-time regular stands before the workbench. They say they are expanding their business and want to commission swords and shields all at once. They offer to pay in advance.
선금만 받고 정해진 수량을 맞춘다: Accept only the deposit and fulfill the set quantity
I delivered the exact quantity. The regular added the remaining payment without a word.
기한을 줄여 더 많이 받는다: Shorten the deadline for a higher price
After working through the night, I delivered it within the deadline. The regular smiled and added another money pouch.
Failed to meet the deadline. I returned the deposit and lost only the material costs.
The regular went to another workshop with a disappointed look.
골목 끝 공방이 문을 닫는다고 한다. 주인이 연장과 재료를 한꺼번에 넘기: The workshop at the end of the alley is closing. The owner wants to sell their tools and materials all at once. There is room to haggle.
재고를 사서 되팔 곳에 넘긴다: Buy the stock and sell it to a reseller
I picked out the usable tools and resold them. It was a profitable deal.
주인과 값을 따져 협상한다: Negotiate the price with the owner
주인은 값을 깎아 준 대신 단골 명단까지 넘겼다. 그 명단이 값어치를 했: The owner lowered the price and handed over their list of regular customers. That list was worth the price.
The negotiation fell through. The owner sold the stock to someone else.
The owner packed the tools into a sack and disappeared into the alley.
협회 보급과에서 사람이 왔다. 한 분기 치 제식 보수 용품을 이 공방에: Someone from the Association's supply department came by. They want to entrust this workshop with the maintenance gear for one quarter. The paperwork is long.
무난한 조건으로 계약한다: Sign the contract under standard terms
I stamped the documents. Delivery took time, but the payment was prompt.
품질 시험을 받고 단가를 올린다: Undergo a quality test to increase unit price
The inspector bent the blade and nodded. The unit price increased.
One item was found defective during the test. The price was reduced.
The documents went back into the bag.
공방에서 만든 시제품 하나가 경매장 도록에 실렸다. 누가 올렸는지는 알: A prototype made in the workshop appeared in an auction catalog. I don't know who listed it. However, the winning bid is set to come to this workshop.
정해진 수수료만 떼고 받는다: Accept after deducting the standard commission
Even after the commission, the amount received was satisfactory.
직접 경매장에 나가 값을 띄운다: Go to the auction house to drive up the price
The price jumped the moment the auctioneer brought down the gavel. Even the onlookers were surprised.
The price did not rise. I only paid the commission.
The catalog was folded and put into the drawer.
해결사 하나가 몰래 찾아왔다. 사정이 있어 공식 공방에는 못 맡기는 장비: A Fixer came to me in secret. They say it is equipment that cannot be taken to an official workshop for personal reasons. The pay is generous. They tell me not to ask why.
I kept my mouth shut and made the repairs. The envelope was as thick as promised.
사정을 캐고 값을 더 부른다: Inquire about the situation and demand a higher price
Once I knew the situation, I was able to demand a higher price. The client paid without a word.
The client caught on. I grabbed my gear and kicked the door open.
I returned the gear. The door remained closed for a long time.
공방 구석에서 먼지 쌓인 설계도 한 묶음이 나왔다. 이 자리에 쌓인 해가: A stack of dusty blueprints was found in the corner of the workshop. They were created over the years spent in this place. Collectors would find them tempting.
한 장씩 팔아 돈으로 바꾼다: Sell them one by one for money
The collector offered a price for each blueprint. The stack turned into money.
전부 모아 한 번에 판다: Collect them all and sell them at once
Once I gathered them all, the value multiplied. The collector even raised the price to buy them.
The collectors just eyed each other and dispersed. Only some were sold.
I bundled the blueprints back up and put them in the corner.
공방 거리 전체가 한 번에 쓸 연장을 주문했다. 이 공방이 가장 믿을 만: The entire Workshop District ordered tools to be used at once. They say this workshop is the most reliable. The volume is enough to fill a whole year.
물량의 일부만 맡는다: Take on only a portion of the order
I took on only what I could handle. The payment came in all at once.
밤낮을 이어 전부 넘겼다. 거리 전체가 이 공방의 이름을 부르며 값을 쳐: I worked day and night to finish it all. The whole district called this workshop's name and paid the price.
I couldn't fulfill the entire order. I paid a portion as a penalty.
The order was transferred to another workshop.
무너진 창고에서 쓸 만한 자재가 쏟아져 나왔다. 주인은 값을 치르지 못한: Useful materials spilled out from the collapsed warehouse. The owner says he can't pay, so he'll hand over all the materials.
자재를 정리해 넘긴다: Sort and hand over the materials
I picked out the useful materials and handed them over. A large sum of money came in.
자재로 신제품을 만들어 판다: Use the materials to make and sell new products
I made and sold new products with the materials. They all sold out at once.
The new products didn't sell well. I barely recovered the cost of the materials.
The materials passed into someone else's hands.
이름을 밝히지 않는 후원자가 공방을 찾았다. 도시 곳곳에서 이 공방의 칼: An anonymous sponsor visited the workshop. They say people all over the City use this workshop's blades. They offered the sponsorship money without conditions.
The sponsorship money arrived in one lump sum. The sponsor left only a greeting instead of a name.
후원자에게 신제품을 보여 주고 더 받는다: Show the sponsor new products to receive more
The sponsor handled the new products and doubled the sponsorship amount.
The sponsor glanced at the new products and paid only the initially promised amount.
The sponsor left without a word. Only an empty cart remained in front of the door.
이제 어디에 몸을 둘지 정해야 한다. 사무소 몇 곳에서 연락이 왔고, 우: Now I must decide where to place myself. Several Offices have reached out, and the mailbox is filled with recruitment notices from Wings and notices from Associations. A syndicate member waits at the corner of the alley.
성공 시 해결사 등록 · 초반 사무소 중에서 고른다 · 실패해도 급이 낮: On success, register as a Fixer · Choose from early Offices · On failure, enter a small, low-tier Office (Yoon · Streetlight)
견습 기간을 버텨 냈다. 서류에 이름이 올라갔고, 어느 문을 두드릴지는: I endured the apprenticeship period. My name is on the documents, and it is up to me to decide which door to knock on.
견습 첫 주에 다쳤지만, 일손이 모자란 작은 사무소가 그래도 받아 주었다: I was injured in the first week of apprenticeship, but a small Office short on hands took me in anyway. My name is on the documents.
합격 시 협회 소속 · 사건 판정 +3 · 카드: On pass, join an Association · Case Check +3 · Card
The examiner stamped the documents. The Association badge is heavier than I thought.
The examiner closed the file. They only said I needed a higher grade.
해결사로 등록된 사람만 심사를 받을 수 있다 · 사무소 견습으로 먼저 등: Only registered Fixers can take the exam · Register as an apprentice first, or if you remain unaffiliated, an Association recommendation letter will arrive
합격 시 최대 HP +8 · 공격 +1 · 카드: On pass, Max HP +8 · Attack +1 · Card
The notice of acceptance arrived. Life inside the walls is quiet and full of regulations.
The exam hall door closed. Only a stack of documents remained in my hands.
손가락의 문을 두드린다: Knock on the door of the Fingers
성공 시 손가락 소속 · 공격 +2 · 카드: On success, join the Fingers · Attack +2 · Card
문이 열렸다. 오늘부터 지켜야 할 규칙이 생겼다. 어기면 손가락 하나로는: The door opened. From today, there are rules I must follow. If I break them, it won't end with just a finger.
There was no answer from beyond the door. I was beaten by someone on the way back.
성공 시 조직 소속(흑운회 · 검계 · 밤의 송곳 중에서 고른다) · 공: On success, join a syndicate (Choose from Kurokumo Clan · Blade Lineage · Night Awl) · Attack +2
The syndicate member at the alley corner nodded. The door opened toward the Backstreets.
따라간 골목 끝에서 아무도 기다리지 않았다. 돌아오는 길에 누군가에게 맞: No one was waiting at the end of the alley I followed. I was beaten by someone on the way back.
It's better to move alone. At least for now.
쌓아 온 실적이 기준에 닿았다. 위에서 심사 일정이 내려왔다. 떨어지면: My accumulated performance has met the criteria. A schedule for the exam has come down from above. If I fail, some of my accumulated performance will be wiped away.
성공 시 승급 · 실패 시 실적 1/4 잃음: On success, promotion · On failure, lose 1/4 of performance
The examiner nodded. I moved up one step.
I fell behind in the practical exam. Some of my performance was erased from the records.
서류와 면접으로 심사를 받는다: Take the exam via documents and interview
The documents and my words matched. I moved up one step.
The interviewer closed the file. Some of my performance was not recognized.
More preparation is needed. Points remain as they are.
1급까지 오른 사람에게만 오는 연락이다. 도시가 당신의 색을 부를지 정하: This contact only comes to those who have reached Grade 1. It is a seat to decide if the City will call your Color. You have up to three chances.
성공 시 특색 · 실패해도 최대 3번까지 도전할 수 있다: Success grants a Color · You may attempt up to 3 times if you fail
The City has begun to call your Color.
The evaluators never shook their heads. The Color did not become a name.
사건 판정 +3 · 최대 HP +4 · 급수 최소 7급: Case Check +3 · Max HP +4 · Grade 7 or higher
공격 +1 · 사건 판정 +3 · 급수 최소 5급: Attack +1 · Case Check +3 · Grade 5 or higher
공격 +1 · 회피 +1 · 최대 HP +6 · 급수 최소 4급: Attack +1 · Evasion +1 · Max HP +6 · Grade 4 or higher
한 해 공적이 정리되어 평가 위원회에 올라갔다. 떨어지면 올해 공적 일부: The year's merits were compiled and submitted to the evaluation committee. If you fail, some of this year's merits will not be recognized.
성공 시 승진 · 실패 시 공적 1/4 잃음: Success promotes you · Failure loses 1/4 of your merit
The field supervisor signed the record. Your rank has increased.
A mistake occurred in the field. Some of your merit was rejected.
The report passed the committee. Your rank has increased.
The report was put on hold. Some of your merit was rejected.
You decided to prepare for another year. What you have built remains.
지부를 맡은 지 얼마 되지 않아 본부에서 사람이 찾아왔다. 협회 전체를: Not long after taking charge of the branch, someone from headquarters visited. They said they would see if you are fit to sit in a position that moves the entire Association. You have up to three chances.
성공 시 칭호 · 실패해도 최대 3번까지 도전할 수 있다: Success grants a title · You may attempt up to 3 times if you fail
Your name has been added to the headquarters documents.
The person from headquarters left without a word. They will not come again.

정리부터 하는 동안 {n}은 옆에서 걸레를 들어 주었다. 일이 끝나자 말: While I cleaned up, {n} picked up a rag to help. When the work was done, they silently held out a glass.
{n}은 당신이 혈귀인 걸 안다. 그런데도 소매를 걷고 상처를 싸매 주며: {n} knows you are a Bloodfiend. Yet, they rolled up their sleeves to bandage your wounds and said, "I wish this were our daily life."
상처를 싸매는 손길이 믿기지 않게 조심스러웠다. 붕대 끝의 매듭이 작은: The touch bandaging my wounds was unbelievably careful. The knot at the end of the bandage was in the shape of a small butterfly.
손을 뺐지만 {n}은 붕대를 다 감을 때까지 기다려 주었다. 이게 일상이: I pulled my hand away, but {n} waited until the bandage was fully wrapped. I heard the words "I wish this were our daily life" once more.
{n}이 마지막 의뢰라며 서류를 내밀었다. 서명란에는 두 사람의 이름이: {n} handed me a document, calling it their final request. Two names were written side by side on the signature line.
두 이름이 나란히 적힌 서류를 {n}이 오래 쓰다듬었다. 마지막 의뢰가: {n} stroked the document with both names side by side for a long time. Their face showed they hoped this final request wouldn't be the last.
서류를 돌려주자 {n}이 알겠다며 접어 넣었다. 접으면서 이 이름 옆자리: When I returned the document, {n} said they understood and folded it away. As they folded it, they whispered that they would leave the seat next to this name empty.
{n}이 칼을 내려놓고 당신 앞에 섰다. 1급 해결사가 이런 얼굴을 한: {n} put down their blade and stood before you. It was the first time I had seen a Grade 1 Fixer look like this.
The Fixer with the blue hair let down became my family. The blade was hung on the wall.
{n}'s final request form returned. Only an obituary was written next to the signature line.
{n}의 의뢰서는 다른 도시로 향했다. 파란 머리는 더 이상 이 골목에서: {n}'s request form headed to another city. The blue hair was no longer seen in this alley.
A Grade 1 Fixer with blue hair tied back.
라만차랜드의 가장 오래된 의자에 앉은 혈귀가 당신을 불렀다. 같은 피를: The Bloodfiend sitting on the oldest chair in L Corp's branch called you over. Another Grade 1, an Elder who shares the same blood. Eyes that have seen hundreds of nights look at you.
{n}이 잔을 내밀었다. 피가 아니라 차였다. 오랜만에 누군가에게 차를: {n} held out a cup. It was tea, not blood. They said it had been a long time since they served tea to anyone.
오랜만에 마시는 차가 이렇게 따뜻한 줄 몰랐다. {n}이 잔을 내려놓으며: I didn't know tea could be this warm after so long. {n} set the cup down and said thank you.
When I pushed the cup away, {n} silently poured fresh, warm water.
{n}은 밤새 지난 시절의 이야기를 했다. 이름을 잃은 혈귀들, 사라진: {n} spent the night telling stories of the past. Bloodfiends who lost their names, chairs that vanished. At the end, {n} called your name.
After listening to stories all night, my heart gave a loud thud the moment my name was called. The old chairs seemed to be watching the two of us.
먼저 일어섰지만 {n}이 문 앞까지 따라와 외투를 걸쳐 주었다. 외투에서: I stood up first, but {n} followed me to the door and draped a coat over my shoulders. The coat smelled of an old scent.
1권속은 피로 약속을 맺는다. {n}이 손목을 내밀었다. 강요는 아니고,: The 1st Progenitor makes an oath with blood. {n} held out their wrist. It wasn't a demand; they were simply waiting.
손목에 닿은 입술이 의외로 따뜻했다. 오랜 의자 하나가 비로소 채워지는: The lips that touched my wrist were unexpectedly warm. I heard the sound of an old chair finally being filled.
시간을 달라고 하자 {n}은 몇 백 년을 기다렸는데 몇 달쯤이야 하며 웃: When I asked for time, {n} laughed, saying they had waited for hundreds of years, so a few months was nothing.
{n}은 수백 번의 밤 끝에서 처음으로 망설이는 얼굴이 되었다. 대답이: At the end of hundreds of nights, {n} wore a hesitant expression for the first time. They need an answer.
오래된 의자 곁에 새 의자가 놓였다. 두 혈귀는 같은 밤을 오래도록 살았: A new chair was placed beside the old one. The two blood-kin lived through the same long night.
Only a red mist remained on {n}'s chair. The long night had ended.
{n}은 오랜 잠을 택해 지하로 내려갔다. 붉은 안개만 한동안 골목에 남: {n} chose a long sleep and went underground. Only a red mist remained in the alley for a while.
A 1st Progenitor elder with eyes that have seen hundreds of nights.
철문 앞의 장신: Tall person before the iron gate
동부 외곽 철문 앞에 키가 큰 금발의 사람이 서 있다. 외곽에서 같이 자: A tall, blonde person stands before the iron gate in the Outskirts. They look as familiar as a face I grew up with in the Outskirts. When our eyes met, they smiled first.
{n}이 아침마다 문 앞에 물을 길어다 놓는다. 이유는 묻지 않았고, 대: {n} draws water and leaves it at my door every morning. I never asked why, and there was no answer.
물동이를 나눠 들자 {n}의 귀 끝이 붉어졌다. 아침 해가 둘의 어깨 위: As we shared the weight of the water bucket, the tips of {n}'s ears turned red. The morning sun sat upon our shoulders together.
모른 척했지만 다음 날부터 물 한 바가지는 내 문 앞에 따로 놓여 있었다: I pretended not to notice, but from the next day on, a bucket of water was left at my door separately.
폭풍이 지나간 밤, {n}이 지붕에 올라 구멍을 막았다. 내려와서는 덜덜: On the night after the storm passed, {n} climbed onto the roof to patch the hole. When they came down, they were shivering and laughing.
{n}, who had been shivering, poked their head out from the blanket and smiled. Their nose was red.
수고했다는 말에 {n}은 한참을 웃었다. 그 한마디가 오늘 가장 따뜻했다: When I told them they did a good job, {n} laughed for a long time. They looked as if that one word was the warmest thing today.
{n}이 옥상에서 별을 가리켰다. 동부에서는 별이 가까이 보인다. 어릴: {n} pointed at the stars from the rooftop. In the East, the stars look closer. It reminded me of the nights we watched together as children.
The stars were close. Leaning my head on {n}'s shoulder was no coincidence.
When I went down first and looked back up, {n} had been watching me longer than the stars.
{n}은 오늘도 문 앞에 서 있다. 올려다봐야 눈이 마주치는 사람이 오늘: {n} is standing at the door again today. The person I have to look up to meet their eyes is avoiding my gaze today.
The tall blonde from the iron gate stepped inside. The morning of the Outskirts became ours.
{n}'s obituary was hung on the iron gate. Only an empty water bucket remained at the door.
{n} left the path before the iron gate. Only an empty water bucket remained at the door.
여관 구석의 사람: Person in the corner of the inn
동부 외곽 여관 구석에 늘 피곤해 보이는 사람이 앉아 있다. 잠을 못 잔: A person who always looks tired sits in the corner of an inn in the Eastern Outskirts. With sleep-deprived eyes, they quietly bow their head whenever you pass by.
{n}이 식은 국을 앞에 두고 졸고 있었다. 숟가락을 쥔 손이 아슬아슬하: {n} was dozing off with cold soup in front of them. The hand holding the spoon was unsteady.
담요를 덮자 졸린 눈이 가늘게 열려 웃었다. 식은 국을 다시 데우는 건: When I covered them with a blanket, their sleepy eyes opened slightly and they smiled. Reheating the cold soup became my job.
지나쳤다가 되돌아와 숟가락을 슬쩍 쥐여 주고 갔다. {n}은 잠결에 고맙: I passed by, then came back to gently place the spoon in their hand. {n} muttered a thank you in their sleep.
{n}은 며칠째 야간 일을 이어 가고 있다. 말 한마디 없이 서 있다가: {n} has been working night shifts for days. They stood without a word before leaning against me and falling asleep.
어깨가 무거워졌지만 싫지 않았다. 숨소리가 고르게 가라앉을 때까지 움직이: My shoulder grew heavy, but I didn't mind. I didn't move until their breathing evened out.
깨워 일으키자 {n}이 부끄러운 듯 웃으며 눈을 비볐다. 잠이 덜 깬 목: When I woke them up, {n} smiled shyly and rubbed their eyes. Their groggy voice was cute.
{n}이 말없이 작은 꾸러미를 내밀었다. 열어 보니 오래 아껴 둔 차였다: {n} silently handed me a small package. When I opened it, it was tea they had cherished for a long time. The shadows under their eyes are a little lighter today.
차가 입안에서 퍼지는 동안 둘 다 말이 없었다. 눈 밑 그늘이 한 겹 더: Neither of us spoke while the tea spread through our mouths. The shadows under their eyes faded by another layer.
고맙다는 말에 {n}이 꾸러미를 한 번 더 쓰다듬었다. 아끼던 차가 처음: At my thanks, {n} stroked the package once more. They looked as if it was the first time they didn't regret using the tea they had cherished.
{n}이 오랜만에 잠들지 않고 앉아 있다. 오늘은 할 말이 있다는 얼굴이: For the first time in a while, {n} is sitting up instead of sleeping. They look as if they have something to say today.
피곤해 보이던 사람이 처음으로 편한 얼굴로 잠들었다. 이제는 곁에 누군가: The person who always looked tired fell asleep with a peaceful face for the first time. Now, there is someone by their side.
{n} did not wake up again. Only the tea package remained by their side.
{n}은 짐을 꾸려 외곽의 더 깊은 곳으로 떠났다. 차 꾸러미 하나를 두: {n} packed their bags and left for a deeper part of the Outskirts. They left one tea package behind.
Their eyes are dark and tired, as if they haven't slept.
검은 정장의 피곤한 눈매의 2급 해결사: A Grade 2 Fixer in a black suit with tired eyes
사무소 복도 끝에서 검은 정장에 넥타이를 맨 해결사가 서류를 넘기고 있다: At the end of the office hallway, a Fixer in a black suit and tie is flipping through documents. Short, dark hair, drooping eyes—a face you could find anywhere. Yet, a Grade 2 Fixer badge is pinned to their chest. When our eyes met, the Fixer smiled tiredly and greeted me first.
{n}과 같은 현장에 배치되었다. 일은 순식간에 끝났다. 장갑 낀 손으로: I was assigned to the same site as {n}. The job was over in an instant. Folding the documents with gloved hands, {n} said that if you do it long enough, your body knows first. They said it as if it were nothing.
나란히 걷는 동안 {n}이 장갑 낀 손으로 서류를 건넸다. 닿지 않았지만: As we walked side by side, {n} handed me the documents with their gloved hand. We didn't touch, but the back of my hand felt warm.
When I left first and looked back, {n} raised their gloved hand in a light wave.
비 오는 날 {n}이 우산도 없이 나타났다. 깔끔하게 빗어 넘긴 머리가: On a rainy day, {n} appeared without an umbrella. Their neatly combed hair was wet and matted. They asked if they could stay by my side for a while, saying they were a bit tired.
젖은 머리를 닦아 주는 손이 서툴렀다. {n}이 눈을 감고 가만히 있어: My hands were clumsy as I dried their wet hair. {n} closed their eyes and stayed still.
문을 닫았다가 다시 열자 {n}은 아직 거기에 서 있었다. 비를 맞으며: When I closed the door and opened it again, {n} was still standing there. They were smiling in the rain.
{n}이 장갑을 벗어 책상에 올려 두었다. 한 번도 벗는 걸 본 적 없는: {n} took off their gloves and placed them on the desk. I had never seen them take them off before. They only said they were a keepsake from someone. It was as if they were showing me their bare hands for the first time.
벗은 손은 생각보다 작고 따뜻했다. 유품이라던 장갑 위에 두 사람의 손이: Their bare hands were smaller and warmer than I thought. Two pairs of hands overlapped on the gloves they called a keepsake.
장갑을 돌려주자 {n}이 가슴에 안았다. 다음에는 장갑 없이 와도 되겠느: When I returned the gloves, {n} held them to their chest. They asked if they could come without gloves next time.
{n}이 장갑 없이 당신 앞에 섰다. 2급 해결사가 이렇게 가벼운 얼굴을: {n} stood before me without gloves. It's the first time I've seen a Grade 2 Fixer look so lighthearted.
검은 정장이 옷장에 한 벌 더 걸렸다. 깔끔하게 빗어 넘기던 머리는 이제: Another black suit was hung in the closet. The hair they used to comb neatly is now disheveled every morning.
{n}의 장갑이 현관에 놓여 있었다. 돌아오지 않은 손이 아직 그 안에: {n}'s gloves were left in the entryway. It felt as if the hand that hadn't returned was still inside them.
{n} left with a job from another office. Only documents remained at the end of the hallway.
검은 정장에 넥타이를 맨, 처진 눈매의 2급 해결사. 늘 장갑을 끼고 있: A Grade 2 Fixer in a black suit and tie with drooping eyes. Always wears gloves.
백발 장발의 특색 1급 해결사: A Color Grade 1 Fixer with long white hair
골목의 소음이 한순간 사라졌다. 흰 장발에 연파란 눈을 가진 해결사가 검: The noise of the alley vanished in an instant. A Fixer with long white hair and pale blue eyes stands there in a black turtleneck. They are a person with a Color, a name even among Grade 1s. Unlike their slender shoulders, their gait is unwavering. Their black leather-gloved hand pointed at you.
{n}과 같은 현장에서 아무 소리도 나지 않았다. 적이 쓰러지고서야 소음: There was no sound at the site with {n}. The noise only returned after the enemy had fallen. {n} adjusted their gloves and said quietly that they hated loud noises.
아무 소리 없는 현장에서 곁에 선 것만으로 충분했다. {n}의 숨소리가: At the silent site, just standing by their side was enough. {n}'s breathing was close.
I left the scene first, but I felt a gaze on my shoulders. It was a warm gaze.
{n}은 늘 검은 옷을 입는다. 이유를 묻자 어디서든 지워지기 쉬워서라고: {n} always wears black clothes. When I asked why, they said it was because it's easy to be erased anywhere. But in front of you, they had the face of someone who didn't want to be erased.
이름을 묻자 {n}이 한참 있다가 작게 대답했다. 아무도 부르지 않는 이: When asked for their name, {n} paused for a long time before answering softly. They said it was a name no one ever called.
묻지 않자 {n}이 더 가까이 다가왔다. 지워지기 쉬운 사람이 오늘은 또: When not asked, {n} stepped closer. The person who was so easy to erase felt vivid today.
{n}이 처음으로 장갑 낀 손을 내밀었다. 무엇이든 꺼낼 수 있는 손이다: {n} reached out a gloved hand for the first time. It was a hand that could pull out anything. This time, they pulled out nothing and simply held your hand.
아무것도 꺼내지 않은 손이 가장 따뜻했다. 맞잡은 손가락 사이로 {n}이: The hand that pulled out nothing was the warmest. {n} smiled through the gaps between your interlaced fingers.
손을 거두자 {n}이 장갑을 다시 끼며 웃었다. 기다리는 것도 괜찮다고: As you withdrew your hand, {n} put their glove back on and smiled. They said waiting was also fine.
{n}이 장갑을 벗지 않은 채로 당신의 손을 잡았다. 주위의 모든 소리가: {n} held your hand without taking off their glove. All surrounding sounds faded, leaving only one person's voice.
백발이 아침 햇살에 풀려 있다. 검은 옷만 입던 사람의 옷장에 색이 하나: White hair flowed in the morning sunlight. A splash of color had appeared in the wardrobe of someone who only wore black.
{n}의 장갑이 식탁 위에 놓여 있었다. 집 안의 모든 소리를 삼키던 장: {n}'s gloves lay on the dining table. The gloves that swallowed every sound in the house had, for the first time, swallowed nothing.
{n}의 자리는 조용히 비었다. 소리 하나 없이 떠나는 일에는 그 사람이: {n}'s seat was quietly empty. That person was more accustomed than anyone to leaving without a sound.
백발 장발에 연파란 눈, 검은 터틀넥과 검은 가죽장갑의 특색 1급 해결사: A Color-grade Fixer with long white hair, pale blue eyes, a black turtleneck, and black leather gloves.
골목에 피보라가 내려앉던 날, 검은 우산 하나가 당신 머리 위로 기울었다: On a day when a blood rain settled over the alley, a black umbrella tilted over your head. Rain that never dried dripped from the tip of the umbrella. They didn't seem to be from the Kurokumo Clan, yet they walked through the organization's territory like it was their own home.
{n}이 우산 하나를 같이 쓰자고 했다. 돌아오는 길 내내 빗물 소리 말: {n} suggested sharing the umbrella. The whole way back, there was nothing but the sound of rain.
빗물 소리만 들리는 길이 이렇게 포근할 줄 몰랐다. 우산 끝에서 떨어지는: I didn't know a road filled only with the sound of rain could be this comforting. The droplets falling from the tip of the umbrella felt like a rhythm.
비를 맞으며 걷자 {n}이 우산을 기울여 따라왔다. 끝내 반쯤 젖은 채: As you walked through the rain, {n} tilted the umbrella to follow you. In the end, you walked side by side, half-drenched.
와카슈에게 넘길 장부가 비에 젖자 {n}이 우산 안쪽에 감싸 말려 주었다: When the ledger to be handed to the Wakashu got wet in the rain, {n} wrapped it inside the umbrella to dry it. They didn't ask why.
고맙다는 말에 {n}이 우산을 한 번 털며 웃었다. 마른 장부가 가슴에: At the word of thanks, {n} shook the umbrella once and smiled. The dry ledger felt warm against your chest.
말없이 장부를 받아 들었다. {n}도 아무 말 없이 우산을 가볍게 흔들었: You accepted the ledger without a word. {n} also shook the umbrella lightly, saying nothing.
조직 일이 끝난 밤, {n}이 우산을 접었다. 하늘은 그날따라 개어 있었: On a night when the organization's work was done, {n} folded the umbrella. The sky had cleared up for once. It was the first time someone stood by your side without an umbrella.
우산 없이 곁에 서는 일이 이렇게 가까운 일이었다. 구름 사이로 달이 둘: Standing side by side without an umbrella felt so close. The moon shone upon the two of you through the clouds.
먼저 걸음을 뗐지만 우산 소리가 바로 뒤에서 따라왔다. 거리는 한 걸음도: You walked away first, but the sound of the umbrella followed right behind. The distance did not widen by even a single step.
우산을 접는 날: The day the umbrella is folded
{n}이 우산을 내밀었다. 손잡이에는 당신 이름이 새겨져 있다. 대답에: {n} held out the umbrella. Your name is engraved on the handle. The shape of this path will change depending on your answer.
검은 우산 하나가 둘의 것이 되었다. 흑운회의 구름 아래에서도 둘이 서는: One black umbrella became something shared by two. Even under the clouds of the Kurokumo Clan, the place where the two stood remained dry.
{n}의 우산이 구름 아래에 펼쳐진 채 남았다. 빗물은 한동안 마르지 않: {n}'s umbrella remained open under the clouds. The rainwater did not dry for a long time.
{n} left the umbrella behind. Your name is still engraved on the handle.
They always carry a black umbrella, and rain that never dries drips from its tip.
마당 한쪽의 칼 닦는 사람: The person cleaning a blade in the yard

{n}이 문 앞에서 밤새 서 있었다. 새벽에 보니 어깨에 이슬이 앉아 있: {n} stood in front of the door all night. At dawn, I saw dew settled on their shoulders. They didn't leave their post even after their shift ended.
문을 열어 안으로 들였다. {n}은 문턱에 한참 서 있다가 방 안쪽 의자: I opened the door and let them in. {n} stood at the threshold for a long time before sitting on the edge of a chair inside. I realized for the first time how quiet the room was.
교대자를 보냈다. 새벽까지 문 밖에서 칼 소리 하나 나지 않았다. 문 앞: I sent them to the shift change. There wasn't a single sound of a blade outside the door until dawn. The dew in front of the door remained wet.

눈짓으로 알렸다. {n}은 잔을 입에 대지 않았다. 후보와 흑수 사이에는: I signaled with a look. {n} didn't bring the cup to their lips. There were more things between the candidate and the Black Hand that didn't need explaining.
{n}이(가) 가주 후보의 자리에서 한 걸음 물러나 앉는다. 흑수에게만: {n} steps back from the candidate's seat. They ask in a voice only the Black Hand can hear: if this seat comes to me, will you stand by my side?

{n}의 이름이 가문의 장부에서 지워졌다. 흑수는 필두의 자리에서 그 이: {n}'s name was erased from the family ledger. The Black Hand called that name for a long time from the lead position.
{n}은 어느 날부터 방 안에 약상자를 놓지 않았다. 문 앞에 서 있던: One day, {n} stopped keeping medicine boxes in the room. Only the spot where the Black Hand stood in front of the door remained.

{n}과 보낸 저녁에는 단말기가 울리지 않았다. 처음에는 반가웠고 곧 불: The terminal didn't ring during the evening I spent with {n}. At first, I was glad, but soon I became anxious. I didn't know that the silence would last this long.

서랍 문을 닫는 소리가 컸다. {n}이 고개를 들었다가 아무 말 없이 다: The sound of the drawer closing was loud. {n} looked up, then picked up the spoon again without a word.
지령에 없던 한마디: A remark not in the directive
{n}이 먼저 입을 열었다. 지령이 무엇이든 상관없다고 한다. 함께 살자: {n} spoke first. They said it didn't matter what the directive was. The words about living together were not in the terminal. For the first time, it was something that didn't need to be written down.

{n}의 자리에 그릇이 하나 비어 있다. 단말기가 서랍 속에서 한 번 울: There is one empty bowl at {n}'s seat. The terminal rang once from inside the drawer. I didn't open it.
{n}은 단말기가 울릴 때마다 표정이 어두워졌다. 어느 날 짐을 싸서 나: {n}'s expression darkened every time the terminal rang. One day, they packed their bags and left. A bowl was overturned on the table.
푸른 눈에 회색 머리를 한 따뜻한 사람이다. 곁에 있으면 지령을 따르는: A warm person with blue eyes and gray hair. Being by their side feels as natural as following a directive.
푸른 눈에 회색 머리를 느슨하게 묶은 사람이다. 지령으로 찾아 나선 상대: A person with blue eyes and gray hair tied loosely. Even though they are someone I sought out due to a directive, they don't feel like a stranger.
